method: Cuba's recreational dive areas: María la Gorda and Guanahacabibes, Cayo Levisa, Havana, Varadero and the Bay of Pigs, Isla de la Juventud with Punta Francés, Cayo Largo, Jardines de la Reina and Santa Lucía in Camagüey. No official list exists: the CNAP park pages, Cuba Travel (the Ministry of Tourism portal) and the state dive operators Marlin, Gaviota and Cubanacán name no individual dive sites, only counts (Marlin Colony 39 sites, Cabo de San Antonio 50, Cayo Largo 32, Santa Lucía about 35; checked on the Marlin site through the Wayback Machine and on the Gaviota and Cuba Travel pages). Named lists exist only on private dive and tour operators, so those were read: Varadero Diving Tour, Varadiving Club, Atlantis Varadero, CubaTopTravel, Cuba Tech Travel (a travel agency that sells the Colony dives), and for Jardines de la Reina Avalon (Cuban Diving Centers), All Star Avalon II and Dive The World, which sell the same Avalon fleet and count as one operator. Travel agencies and receptive operators that sell dive packages were counted as operator lists, which is a looser reading than elsewhere, because no dive center in the country publishes its own. A site is counted when named on at least two independent lists. That leaves five counted sites: Coral Beach and the Bay of Pigs shore dive (three Varadero operators) and the three Punta Francés sites on the two Isla de la Juventud agency lists. Jardines de la Reina has a single operator, Avalon, so all its sites are excluded under the counting rule; María la Gorda's sites sit on one agency list and an unofficial guide (cubadiving.org, a personal website that reproduces a 39-site map and was not counted), so they are excluded too; this denominator is therefore a floor, not a census. Magazines, blogs, PADI, EcuRed and travel-guide sites were used for leads only. No list gave coordinates. Counted 2026-10-14.
